description: Catalog of individual code-style flags (naming, braces, indentation, imports, comments, and language-specific conventions). Each flag is an independently toggleable rule that an LLM applies when generating or refactoring code. Presets in programming-styles-presets.json reference these flagId values.

fields.flagId: Stable snake_case identifier referenced by presets and project config.
fields.name: Human-readable flag name.
fields.group: Organisational grouping (naming, braces, indentation, line_length, whitespace, imports, comments, types, csharp, cpp, python, javascript, typescript, uxml, uss, shader).
fields.llmRule: The instruction the LLM must follow when this flag is enabled.
fields.whenToUse: Situations or language ecosystems where the flag is a good fit.

flags.name: Class names in PascalCase
flags.description: Type names (classes, structs, records) are written in PascalCase.
flags.llmRule: Name classes, structs, and records in PascalCase.
flags.whenToUse: C#, C++, TypeScript, and other languages whose type conventions use PascalCase.

flags.name: Class names in snake_case
flags.description: Type names are written in snake_case.
flags.llmRule: Name classes in snake_case.
flags.whenToUse: Python, some C++ codebases, and projects that standardise on snake_case types.

flags.name: Function names in PascalCase
flags.description: Methods and functions are written in PascalCase.
flags.llmRule: Name methods and functions in PascalCase.
flags.whenToUse: C# methods, C++ methods in PascalCase style guides, and some C++/Unreal codebases.

flags.name: Function names in camelCase
flags.description: Methods and functions are written in camelCase.
flags.llmRule: Name methods and functions in camelCase.
flags.whenToUse: JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, and C# locals/parameters.

flags.name: Function names in snake_case
flags.description: Functions are written in snake_case.
flags.llmRule: Name functions in snake_case.
flags.whenToUse: Python, C, and C++ codebases that follow snake_case function conventions.

flags.name: Variable names in camelCase
flags.description: Local variables and parameters are written in camelCase.
flags.llmRule: Name local variables and parameters in camelCase.

flags.name: Variable names in snake_case
flags.description: Local variables and parameters are written in snake_case.
flags.llmRule: Name local variables and parameters in snake_case.
flags.whenToUse: Python, C, C++, and shader code.

flags.name: Constants in UPPER_SNAKE_CASE
flags.description: Compile-time constants are written in UPPER_SNAKE_CASE.
flags.llmRule: Name constants in UPPER_SNAKE_CASE.
flags.whenToUse: C, C++, Python module constants, and JS/TS module constants.

flags.name: Constants in PascalCase
flags.description: Compile-time constants are written in PascalCase.
flags.llmRule: Name constants in PascalCase.
flags.whenToUse: C# const fields and some TypeScript enum-style constants.

flags.name: Private members prefixed with underscore
flags.description: Private fields are prefixed with a single underscore.
flags.llmRule: Prefix private fields with a single underscore.
flags.whenToUse: C#, Python, and JS/TS private-by-convention codebases.

flags.name: Private members prefixed with m_
flags.description: Private fields are prefixed with m_.
flags.llmRule: Prefix private fields with m_.
flags.whenToUse: Legacy C#/Unity and C++ codebases that use member prefixes.

flags.name: Private members suffixed with underscore
flags.description: Private member variables are suffixed with a trailing underscore.
flags.llmRule: Suffix private member variables with a trailing underscore.
flags.whenToUse: C++ codebases such as Google C++ style.

flags.name: Interfaces prefixed with I
flags.description: Interfaces are named with a leading I.
flags.llmRule: Prefix interface names with I.

flags.name: Interfaces without I prefix
flags.description: Interfaces are named without a leading I.
flags.llmRule: Do not prefix interface names with I; use a descriptive adjective or noun.

flags.name: Type names in PascalCase
flags.description: All type declarations (class, struct, enum, delegate, record) use PascalCase.
flags.llmRule: Name all types in PascalCase.

flags.name: Enum type names in PascalCase
flags.description: Enum type names use PascalCase, usually singular.
flags.llmRule: Name enum types in PascalCase and prefer singular names.

flags.name: Enum members in PascalCase
flags.description: Enum members use PascalCase.
flags.llmRule: Name enum members in PascalCase.

flags.name: Enum members in UPPER_SNAKE_CASE
flags.description: Enum members use UPPER_SNAKE_CASE.
flags.llmRule: Name enum members in UPPER_SNAKE_CASE.
flags.whenToUse: C, C++, and some Python codebases.

flags.name: Properties in PascalCase
flags.description: Property names use PascalCase.
flags.llmRule: Name properties in PascalCase.

flags.name: Events in PascalCase
flags.description: Event names use PascalCase, often past-tense or with an On prefix.
flags.llmRule: Name events in PascalCase, using past-tense or an On prefix consistently.

flags.name: Boolean names use is/has/can
flags.description: Boolean members and locals are prefixed with is, has, can, or should.
flags.llmRule: Prefix boolean names with is, has, can, or should.

flags.name: Async methods suffixed with Async
flags.description: Asynchronous methods are suffixed with Async.
flags.llmRule: Suffix asynchronous methods with Async.
flags.whenToUse: C#, JavaScript, and TypeScript async APIs.

flags.name: File named after its primary type
flags.description: Each file is named after the primary type it contains.
flags.llmRule: Name each file after the primary type it contains.
flags.whenToUse: C#, Java, and TypeScript class-per-file conventions.

flags.name: Files in snake_case
flags.description: Source file names use snake_case.
flags.llmRule: Name files in snake_case.

flags.name: Namespaces in PascalCase
flags.description: Namespaces use PascalCase.
flags.llmRule: Name namespaces in PascalCase.

flags.name: Namespaces in snake_case
flags.description: Namespaces and packages use snake_case.
flags.llmRule: Name namespaces and packages in snake_case.

flags.name: Behavioural test names
flags.description: Tests are named method_scenario_expected using underscores.
flags.llmRule: Name tests method_scenario_expected using underscores and describe the behaviour, not the implementation.

flags.name: Generic parameters prefixed with T
flags.description: Generic type parameters are prefixed with T.
flags.llmRule: Prefix generic type parameters with T (for example TItem).

flags.name: Callbacks use On prefix
flags.description: Callback members use an On prefix and handlers use a matching suffix.
flags.llmRule: Name callback members with an On prefix and handlers with a matching suffix.
flags.whenToUse: Unity C# event and callback systems.

flags.name: Function braces on same line
flags.description: The opening brace of a function body is on the same line as the signature.
flags.llmRule: Place the opening brace of a function on the same line as its signature.
flags.whenToUse: K&R / one-true-brace style used by JavaScript, Java, and many C# teams.

flags.name: Function braces on next line
flags.description: The opening brace of a function body is on the next line.
flags.llmRule: Place the opening brace of a function on the next line.
flags.whenToUse: Allman style used by Microsoft C# and many C++ codebases.

flags.name: Control braces on same line
flags.description: Opening braces of if/for/while/switch are on the same line.
flags.llmRule: Place the opening brace of a control statement on the same line.

flags.name: Control braces on next line
flags.description: Opening braces of if/for/while/switch are on the next line.
flags.llmRule: Place the opening brace of a control statement on the next line.

flags.name: Type braces on same line
flags.description: Opening braces of type declarations are on the same line.
flags.llmRule: Place the opening brace of a type declaration on the same line.

flags.name: Type braces on next line
flags.description: Opening braces of type declarations are on the next line.
flags.llmRule: Place the opening brace of a type declaration on the next line.
flags.whenToUse: Allman style and default C# formatting.

flags.name: Always use braces
flags.description: Control-statement bodies always use braces, even for a single statement.
flags.llmRule: Always wrap control-statement bodies in braces, even for a single statement.

flags.name: Allow braceless single statements
flags.description: Braces may be omitted when the body is a single statement.
flags.llmRule: Braces may be omitted only when the body is exactly one statement.
flags.whenToUse: Only when the project explicitly permits braceless bodies.

flags.name: Empty blocks as {}
flags.description: Empty blocks are written as {} on one line.
flags.llmRule: Write empty blocks as {}.

flags.name: Single brace style per file
flags.description: Brace placement never mixes within a file.
flags.llmRule: Use exactly one brace placement style throughout a file.

flags.name: Indent with 4 spaces
flags.description: One indentation level is four spaces.
flags.llmRule: Indent with four spaces per level.
flags.whenToUse: C#, Java, Python (PEP 8), C++, and shader code.

flags.name: Indent with 2 spaces
flags.description: One indentation level is two spaces.
flags.llmRule: Indent with two spaces per level.
flags.whenToUse: JavaScript, TypeScript, UXML, USS, and XML/HTML.

flags.name: Indent with tabs
flags.description: Indentation uses hard tabs.
flags.llmRule: Indent with hard tabs.
flags.whenToUse: Projects that mandate tabs (some C/C++/Go codebases).

flags.name: Never mix tabs and spaces
flags.description: A file uses either tabs or spaces, never both.
flags.llmRule: Never mix tabs and spaces for indentation in the same file.

flags.name: Wrap at 80 columns
flags.description: Lines are wrapped at 80 columns.
flags.llmRule: Wrap lines at 80 columns.
flags.whenToUse: Python (PEP 8), C, and strict style guides.

flags.name: Wrap at 100 columns
flags.description: Lines are wrapped at 100 columns.
flags.llmRule: Wrap lines at 100 columns.

flags.name: Wrap at 120 columns
flags.description: Lines are wrapped at 120 columns.
flags.llmRule: Wrap lines at 120 columns.

flags.name: Strip trailing whitespace
flags.description: No line ends with trailing whitespace.
flags.llmRule: Remove trailing whitespace from every line.

flags.name: End file with newline
flags.description: Every file ends with exactly one newline.
flags.llmRule: End every file with exactly one newline.

flags.name: Space after commas
flags.description: A single space follows each comma and none precedes it.
flags.llmRule: Put one space after commas and none before.

flags.name: Spaces around operators
flags.description: Binary operators are surrounded by single spaces.
flags.llmRule: Put spaces around binary operators.

flags.name: No space before call parentheses
flags.description: Function calls have no space between the name and the opening parenthesis.
flags.llmRule: Do not put a space between a function name and its call parentheses.

flags.name: Space before control parentheses
flags.description: Control keywords are followed by a space before the parenthesis.
flags.llmRule: Put a space between control keywords (if, for, while, switch) and their parentheses.

flags.name: Blank line between members
flags.description: Type members are separated by a single blank line.
flags.llmRule: Separate type members with a single blank line.

flags.name: At most two blank lines
flags.description: No more than two consecutive blank lines.
flags.llmRule: Never use more than two consecutive blank lines.

flags.name: Align consecutive assignments
flags.description: Consecutive assignment operators are vertically aligned.
flags.llmRule: Vertically align the assignment operators of consecutive declarations.
flags.whenToUse: Codebases that opt into aligned declaration blocks.

flags.name: Sort imports alphabetically
flags.description: Import/using directives are sorted alphabetically.
flags.llmRule: Sort import and using directives alphabetically.

flags.name: Group imports by origin
flags.description: Imports are grouped by standard library, third-party, and local, separated by blank lines.
flags.llmRule: Group imports into standard library, third-party, and local groups separated by blank lines.

flags.name: Usings outside namespace
flags.description: Using directives appear before the namespace declaration.
flags.llmRule: Place using directives outside the namespace.

flags.name: Usings inside namespace
flags.description: Using directives appear inside the namespace declaration.
flags.llmRule: Place using directives inside the namespace.

flags.name: No wildcard imports
flags.description: Imports name specific symbols and never use wildcards.
flags.llmRule: Import specific symbols; never use wildcard imports.

flags.name: Remove unused imports
flags.description: Unused imports/usings are removed.
flags.llmRule: Remove every unused import and using directive.

flags.name: Document the public API
flags.description: Every public type and member has a documentation comment.
flags.llmRule: Document every public type and member with a doc comment.

flags.name: XML doc comments
flags.description: Documentation uses XML comments with summary/param/returns.
flags.llmRule: Use XML doc comments with summary, param, and returns tags.

flags.name: Google-style docstrings
flags.description: Python docstrings follow Google style.
flags.llmRule: Write Python docstrings in Google style.

flags.name: NumPy-style docstrings
flags.description: Python docstrings follow NumPy style.
flags.llmRule: Write Python docstrings in NumPy style.

flags.name: PEP 257 docstrings
flags.description: Python docstrings follow PEP 257.
flags.llmRule: Follow PEP 257 for Python docstrings.

flags.name: No commented-out code
flags.description: Commented-out code is never committed.
flags.llmRule: Never leave commented-out code; delete it because version control keeps history.

flags.name: Comments explain why
flags.description: Comments explain intent and rationale, not mechanics.
flags.llmRule: Write comments that explain why, not what; let the code explain what.

flags.name: Structured TODO comments
flags.description: TODOs follow the form TODO(owner): reason.
flags.llmRule: Format TODOs as TODO(owner): reason.

flags.name: Section divider comments
flags.description: Long files separate logical sections with divider comments.
flags.llmRule: Use divider comments to separate logical sections in long files.
flags.whenToUse: Shaders, large classes, and long configuration files.

flags.name: Explicit types over inference
flags.description: Variable declarations use explicit types rather than inference.
flags.llmRule: Prefer explicit types over inferred types.
flags.whenToUse: C# and TypeScript teams that value readability.

flags.name: Use var when obvious
flags.description: Type inference is used when the type is obvious from the right-hand side.
flags.llmRule: Use var when the type is obvious from the right-hand side; otherwise use the explicit type.

flags.name: Explicit return types
flags.description: Function return types are always written explicitly.
flags.llmRule: Always annotate function return types explicitly.

flags.name: Strict equality
flags.description: Strict equality operators are used instead of loose ones.
flags.llmRule: Use === and !== instead of == and !=.

flags.name: Prefer const
flags.description: const is preferred; let is used only when reassignment is needed; var is never used.
flags.llmRule: Prefer const; use let only when reassignment is required; never use var.

flags.name: Prefer arrow functions
flags.description: Arrow functions are used for callbacks.
flags.llmRule: Prefer arrow functions for callbacks.

flags.name: Strict null checks
flags.description: Nullability is tracked and enforced.
flags.llmRule: Honour strict null checks and handle null/undefined explicitly.
flags.whenToUse: TypeScript and C# nullable reference types.

flags.name: Immutable by default
flags.description: Fields and locals are immutable unless reassignment is required.
flags.llmRule: Mark fields and locals readonly/const/final unless they must change.

flags.name: C# nullable reference types
flags.description: Nullable reference types are enabled and annotated.
flags.llmRule: Enable nullable reference types and annotate nullability.

flags.name: C# expression-bodied members
flags.description: Simple properties and methods use expression bodies.
flags.llmRule: Use expression-bodied members for simple properties and methods.

flags.name: C# file-scoped namespaces
flags.description: Namespaces are declared with the file-scoped syntax.
flags.llmRule: Use file-scoped namespace declarations.

flags.name: C# sealed by default
flags.description: Classes are sealed unless designed for inheritance.
flags.llmRule: Mark classes sealed unless they are explicitly designed for inheritance.

flags.name: C# readonly fields
flags.description: Fields that are not reassigned are marked readonly.
flags.llmRule: Mark fields readonly when they are not reassigned.

flags.name: C# nameof
flags.description: nameof is used instead of string literals for member names.
flags.llmRule: Use nameof instead of string literals for member names.

flags.name: C# attributes on their own line
flags.description: Attributes are placed on their own line above the member.
flags.llmRule: Place attributes on their own line above the member.

flags.name: C# string interpolation
flags.description: String interpolation is preferred over concatenation or string.Format.
flags.llmRule: Prefer string interpolation over concatenation or string.Format.

flags.name: C# pattern matching
flags.description: Pattern matching and switch expressions are preferred over nested conditionals.
flags.llmRule: Prefer pattern matching and switch expressions over nested if/else chains.

flags.name: C# avoid regions
flags.description: #region blocks are avoided in favour of smaller files.
flags.llmRule: Avoid #region; split the file instead.

flags.name: Unity private serialized fields
flags.description: Inspector fields are private and marked [SerializeField].
flags.llmRule: Mark Unity inspector fields [SerializeField] private.

flags.name: C++ const correctness
flags.description: Methods and parameters are marked const wherever possible.
flags.llmRule: Mark methods and parameters const wherever possible.

flags.name: C++ use auto
flags.description: auto is used when the type is obvious or unwieldy.
flags.llmRule: Use auto when the type is obvious from the initialiser or is unwieldy to write.

flags.name: C++ explicit constructors
flags.description: Single-argument constructors are marked explicit.
flags.llmRule: Mark single-argument constructors explicit.

flags.name: C++ override and final
flags.description: Virtual overrides are marked override and non-inheritable methods final.
flags.llmRule: Mark virtual overrides with override and non-inheritable methods with final.

flags.name: C++ #pragma once
flags.description: Headers use #pragma once instead of include guards.
flags.llmRule: Use #pragma once instead of include guards.

flags.name: C++ no using namespace in headers
flags.description: Headers never contain using namespace directives.
flags.llmRule: Never put using namespace directives in headers.

flags.name: C++ smart pointers
flags.description: Owning pointers are smart pointers rather than raw pointers.
flags.llmRule: Prefer smart pointers over raw owning pointers.

flags.name: C++ include order
flags.description: Includes are ordered matching header, C standard, C++ standard, third-party, local.
flags.llmRule: Order includes as matching header, C standard, C++ standard, third-party, then local.

flags.name: C++ pointer alignment
flags.description: The pointer/reference marker binds to the type, not the variable.
flags.llmRule: Bind * and & to the type, not the variable name.
flags.whenToUse: C++ codebases that prefer type-bound declarators.

flags.name: Python PEP 8
flags.description: Code follows PEP 8.
flags.llmRule: Follow PEP 8.

flags.name: Python Black-compatible
flags.description: Formatting is compatible with Black.
flags.llmRule: Keep formatting compatible with Black.

flags.name: Python type hints
flags.description: Function signatures are annotated with type hints.
flags.llmRule: Annotate function signatures with type hints.

flags.name: Python double quotes
flags.description: Strings use double quotes.
flags.llmRule: Prefer double quotes for strings.

flags.name: Python f-strings
flags.description: f-strings are used for interpolation.
flags.llmRule: Prefer f-strings for string interpolation.

flags.name: Python main guard
flags.description: Script entry points are guarded with if __name__ == '__main__'.
flags.llmRule: Guard script entry with if __name__ == '__main__'.

flags.name: Python private underscore
flags.description: Internal names are prefixed with a single underscore.
flags.llmRule: Prefix internal names with a single underscore.

flags.name: JavaScript semicolons
flags.description: Statements are terminated with semicolons.
flags.llmRule: Terminate statements with semicolons.
flags.whenToUse: JavaScript and TypeScript projects that require semicolons.

flags.name: JavaScript no semicolons
flags.description: Semicolons are omitted and rely on automatic semicolon insertion.
flags.llmRule: Omit semicolons; rely on automatic semicolon insertion consistently.
flags.whenToUse: JavaScript projects using Prettier with semi: false.

flags.name: JavaScript single quotes
flags.description: Strings use single quotes.
flags.llmRule: Use single quotes for strings.
flags.whenToUse: JavaScript and TypeScript projects using Prettier defaults.

flags.name: JavaScript double quotes
flags.description: Strings use double quotes.
flags.llmRule: Use double quotes for strings.
flags.whenToUse: JavaScript and TypeScript projects that standardise on double quotes.

flags.name: ES module imports
flags.description: Code uses ES module import/export syntax.
flags.llmRule: Use ES module import and export syntax.

flags.name: async/await
flags.description: async/await is preferred over promise chains.
flags.llmRule: Prefer async/await over promise chains.

flags.name: TypeScript type over interface
flags.description: Type aliases are preferred over interfaces unless declaration merging is needed.
flags.llmRule: Prefer type aliases over interfaces unless declaration merging is required.
flags.whenToUse: TypeScript codebases that prefer type aliases.

flags.name: TypeScript no any
flags.description: any is forbidden; unknown and narrowing are used instead.
flags.llmRule: Do not use any; prefer unknown and narrow it explicitly.

flags.name: TypeScript unions over enums
flags.description: String literal unions are preferred over enums.
flags.llmRule: Prefer string literal unions over enums.
flags.whenToUse: TypeScript codebases that avoid runtime enums.

flags.name: TypeScript strict mode
flags.description: The compiler runs with strict: true.
flags.llmRule: Assume and preserve strict mode; do not weaken compiler options.

flags.name: UXML indent 2 spaces
flags.description: UXML is indented with two spaces.
flags.llmRule: Indent UXML with two spaces per level.

flags.name: UXML one attribute per line
flags.description: Elements with several attributes place each on its own line.
flags.llmRule: Place each attribute on its own line when an element has more than two attributes.

flags.name: UXML/USS BEM class names
flags.description: USS class names follow a BEM-like block__element--modifier convention.
flags.llmRule: Name USS classes using a BEM-like block__element--modifier convention.
flags.whenToUse: Unity UI Toolkit UXML and USS.

flags.name: UXML classes over inline styles
flags.description: USS classes are used instead of inline style attributes.
flags.llmRule: Use USS classes instead of inline style attributes.

flags.name: USS property order
flags.description: USS properties are ordered consistently, typically box model outward.
flags.llmRule: Order USS properties consistently, box model outward.

flags.name: USS variables
flags.description: USS custom properties are used for colours and spacing.
flags.llmRule: Use USS custom properties (variables) for colours and spacing.

flags.name: USS no !important
flags.description: !important is avoided.
flags.llmRule: Avoid !important.

flags.name: USS low specificity
flags.description: Selectors keep specificity low.
flags.llmRule: Keep USS selector specificity low; prefer single classes.

flags.name: USS consistent units
flags.description: Units are used consistently (px for fixed, % for fluid).
flags.llmRule: Use px for fixed sizes and % for fluid sizes consistently.

flags.name: Shader indent 4 spaces
flags.description: Shader code is indented with four spaces.
flags.llmRule: Indent shader code with four spaces per level.

flags.name: Shader uniforms prefixed
flags.description: Global uniforms are prefixed with an underscore.
flags.llmRule: Prefix global uniform names with an underscore.

flags.name: Shader properties PascalCase
flags.description: Shader properties use PascalCase with a leading underscore for the reference.
flags.llmRule: Name shader properties in PascalCase and reference them with a leading underscore.

flags.name: Shader braces next line
flags.description: Opening braces are placed on the next line.
flags.llmRule: Place opening braces on the next line.

flags.name: Shader section comments
flags.description: Section banners separate Properties, SubShader, Pass, and HLSLINCLUDE.
flags.llmRule: Use section comment banners to separate Properties, SubShader, Pass, and HLSLINCLUDE.

flags.name: Shader prefer half precision
flags.description: half/min16float is used for colour math on mobile.
flags.llmRule: Prefer half or min16float for colour math on mobile targets.

flags.name: Shader avoid branching
flags.description: Dynamic branching is avoided in fragment shaders.
flags.llmRule: Avoid dynamic branching in fragment shaders; prefer lerp and step.
